text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German Bund futures were hit by profit-taking and a weaker Treasury market on Monday after posting sharp gains late last week. Traders said they remain bullish on the contract, but that with German economic data due on Wednesday, they were reluctant to add to what has been a 140 basis point gain over the last two weeks. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 102.41, down 0.15 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - December gilt futures settled just off their new contract high on Monday following a modest rally spurred by a soft November manufacturing survey. The market was a little better bid today with some decent numbers, though trading was very, very quiet. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-31/32, up 4/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures overcame early jitters after a surprise fall in unemployment in November to set a new contract high, trimming benchmark 10-year government bond yields to their lowest level in more than two decades. The December bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.42 up 0.26 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian cash bonds closed down but futures put in a more resilient performance, ending around 20 basis points higher on the day, just short of the recent record peak on the December contract. There was some small profit-taking but once it came back to positive ground, technical buying set in, one broker in London said, noting Italian bond futures had managed to keep their head above water even when Bunds dropped back. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.03 up 0.19 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened lower on Monday as investors took profits after Friday's advance. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-21/32, down 7/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.37 percent.

JAPAN - Cash Japanese government bonds (JGB) extended gains into uncharted waters with the benchmark yield falling to a record low 2.350 percent in a buying spree led by both investors and dealers. In after hours trading the March uture on LIFFE was trading at 126.47, up 0.67 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - LONDON - The primary market saw little action on Monday, with an opportunistic dollar deal from NV Bank Nederlandse Gemeenten (BNG) adding some life. BNG launched a $200 million four-year bond to yield two basis points over the interpolated U.S. Treasury curves. A syndicate official at lead manager Paribas Capital Markets said the bond was an opportunistic offering given the dearth of paper in the four-year dollar sector.
